catalog_quote: Bwala has two distinctive tones, high (H) and low (L). When it comes to disyllabic noun stems, the distinctive tone patterns are H-HL and L-LL, e.g. dí-ínì/mí-ínì ‘tooth’ and mù-sùnù/mì-sùnù ‘meat’. For noun stems which have more than two syllables, Bwala appears to have two distinctive tone patterns: H-HHL or H-HLL. L-LLL noun stems do not occur in our data. Noun class prefixes in Bwala carry either a H or a L tone. Noun stems with a HL tone pattern have a H- toned noun class prefix, whereas the prefix preceding LL noun stems has a L tone. This tonal behaviour has a diachronic explanation. Noun class prefixes in Bwala first underwent leftward H tone spread within the word. Afterwards, the common Bantu tonal dissimilation process known as “Meeussen’s Rule” (Marlo and Odden 2019, 151, 157) transforms *HH into HL within the noun stem.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: The quoted passage is verbatim in, but it sits at the top of p. 5 (of 40) (extracted text; page footer "5 (40)"), not p. 4 as the locator says; §2 "Preliminary account of Bwala phonology" begins on p. 4 (five vowels, consonant Table 1) and continues on p. 5 with the tone paragraph. Only difference is the page number. READING: The whole of §2 (pp. 4-5) treats vowels, consonants and a two-tone (H/L) system with H-tone spread and Meeussen's Rule; the only hits for stress/accent/prominence in the entire article are p. 20 (not p. 25; footer "20 (40)") "the stem-initial position is a position of phonetic and phonological prominence in Teke languages (Paulian 1975)" -- a general Teke remark…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Two-tone (H/L) language; the phonology sketch describes lexical tone patterns on noun stems and prefixes and says nothing about word stress or accent. For Mfinu proper, Daeleman 1977 (comparative study, p. 96) likewise only reports 'tonally marked Mfinu (B.83) correspondents' and states that a systematic study of the sounds and phonemes was impossible.
new_statements.exceptions: None about stress. The same paper (p. 25) notes in passing that 'the stem-initial position is a position of phonetic and phonological prominence in Teke languages (Paulian 1975)', a general Teke claim drawn from Kukuya (B73), not a Bwala/Mfinu stress rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Noun stems and noun-class prefixes in isolation (citation forms, one main consultant, Bankana 2018-2019). No statement about phrase-level prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Bwala (provisional Guthrie code B70z; villages Ngaana, Kingao, Bankana, Kinshasa Province), which Glottolog 5.1 subsumes under mfin1238 (its refs 586239/586240 are coded 'Bwala B70z = Mfinu [zmf]') but which Kouarata, Pacchiarotti & Bostoen 2023 list separately from Mfinu B83 (Bingibingi, Yuo, Bita) as a distinct variety within the Teke continuum; no separate glottocode exists for Bwala. For Mfinu proper (B83) the only accessible first-hand evidence is Daeleman 1977, whose tone-marked data confirm a tone language but carry no phonological description. Mfinu is filed by Guthrie/Maho under B80 Tiene-Yanzi, yet Pacchiarotti et al. 2019 and Kouarata et al. 2023 treat it as part of the Teke (B70) dialect continuum.

sources.note: §2 'Preliminary account of Bwala phonology' (p. 4): five vowels, consonant table, 'Bwala has two distinctive tones, high (H) and low (L)' with H-HL / L-LL stem patterns; no mention of stress or accent anywhere. p. 25 remarks that 'the stem-initial position is a position of phonetic and phonological prominence in Teke languages (Paulian 1975)'. Glottolog 5.1 files Bwala (B70z) under mfin1238; the authors treat it as 'a distinct variety within a larger Teke dialect continuum'.

sources.note: pp. 173-174: Mfinu (B83) spoken east of Kinshasa, not usually classified as Teke referentially; speakers also called Bamfununga, Munika, Mfono (Guthrie 1953: 81; 1956: 84; Boone 1973: 229). Phylogeny places Mfinu in the Kasai-Ngounie (Extended) subclade with Bwala. Nothing on prosody.
